subject: Implementation Questionnaire & Migration Plan — Globex Financial RFP
content:
From: Henry Li <henry.li@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@globex.com>, procurement@globex.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Globex RFP: Implementation questionnaire and desired migration timeline

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our RFP evaluation we need a quick, written response to the implementation section (questions attached). Specifically we want:

- A proposed migration timeline for a 3-environment rollout (staging -> pilot -> prod) including estimated engineering effort and calendar duration.
- A high-level integration checklist for our platform (authentication, data residency, audit logs, KV cache behavior).
- Canary/traffic-split approaches you recommend (criteria, duration, rollback triggers).

Please complete the attached XLSX and send any supporting plan PDFs. Our procurement/legal team will also want to see SLA and onboarding milestones. Target timeline for decision is end of May — so if you can get this back early next week that would be ideal.

Attachment: Globex_RFP_Implementation_Questions.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 48KB)

Regards,
Henry Li
Director, Vendor Evaluation | Globex Financial
henry.li@globex.com

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Henry Li <henry.li@globex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Globex RFP: Implementation questionnaire and desired migration timeline

Henry —

Thanks, received. We completed the attached workbook with per-question responses and are including a first-pass implementation plan (attached PDF). High-level notes below, and I’ve looped in Karthik and Laura for the technical and procurement parts.

High-level proposed timeline (calendar):
- Week 0–2: Kickoff, architecture alignment, contract signature and SSO provisioning.
- Week 3–5: Private onboarding: VPC peering, test data flow, basic auth and KMS integration.
- Week 6–8: Pilot deployment — run 2 weeks of production-like traffic with 10% canary.
- Week 9–11: Post-pilot tuning, quantization/profile adjustments, documentation handoff.
- Week 12: Prod cutover and 4-week monitoring/rollback window.

Estimated engineering effort: 4–6 FTE-weeks across infra and integration engineers for the pilot; smaller ongoing ops for production. Exact effort depends on the target throughput and whether you require on-prem gateways for audit capture.

Canary approach (initial recommendation):
- Canary size: 5–15% depending on traffic profiles.
- Duration: minimum 48–72 hours of steady-state traffic or ~100k inference tokens served (whichever is longer).
- Success criteria: error rate < 0.5% above baseline, 95th percentile latency within SLA band, and model-quality checks (sampled prompts & eval set pass).
- Rollback triggers: elevated error rates, latency regressions exceeding 2x baseline, or model-quality drift detected by the eval hooks.

Attaching: Implementation-Plan-v1.pdf (overview + milestone Gantt) and the completed XLSX per your RFP.

Next steps: Karthik, can you add the network/integration checklist items and any prerequisites for SOC-level evidence? Laura, procurement items (SLA milestones, onboarding credits) — anything to call out to Henry?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Implementation-Plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
[Attachment: Globex_RFP_Implementation_Questions.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 48KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Henry Li <henry.li@globex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Globex RFP: Implementation questionnaire and desired migration timeline

Henry — adding the technical integration checklist and a few clarifying notes:

Integration checklist (network & infra):
- Authentication: SAML OIDC handshake for user auth; we support SCIM for user provisioning. Need SP metadata from your IdP.
- Networking: Support for VPC peering or PrivateLink; we recommend dedicated subnets for inference nodes. Public-hosted option also available if isolation not required.
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ between client and Redwood public endpoints; explicit option for customer-managed TLS via HSM for Private deployments.
- Data at rest: Model KV cache stored on ephemeral GPU memory; persistent logs and audit trail are pushed to a customer-owned S3 bucket (or compatible object store). Provide bucket ARN and IAM role for write access.
- Audit logs: We emit request/response metadata (headers, tokens served count, latency) to your audit pipeline. We can extend to push full request IDs on demand.
- KV cache warming: For large-model warmstart (long history tasks), we recommend a pre-warm sequence during pilot to avoid initial latency spikes.

Operational prerequisites:
- Service account with IAM permissions for S3/KMS as above.
- Firewall rules: outbound to our egress IP range (list to be provided) for hosted mode.
- Test dataset: a synthetic dataset with representative sequences for quality checks during pilot.

Canary specifics (technical):
- Traffic split handled by our routing layer; we can set client-side header + routing key to steer X% of traffic.
- Telemetry: We’ll provide per-token cost and latency metrics per route. Integrate those into your observability workspace for the pilot.

Attachment references: I’ve added a canary-schedule-template.csv to the shared plan with a sample 2-week ramp.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Platform Integrations | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

[Attachment: canary-schedule-template.csv (CSV, 2KB)]

Henry —

Procurement/contracting notes:
- Typical SLA start: SLA clock begins at production cutover; we propose a 99.5% availability target for the first 6 months with quarterly reporting.
- Onboarding credits: For pilot customers we often include 2 weeks of reserved capacity credits to smooth the pilot.
- Contracting items your legal team commonly requests: data retention window, indemnity carveouts, and audit access for SOC reports. We can surface SOC 2 Type II evidence and a sample DPIA for EU data controls.

For the RFP sheet we added estimates for milestone acceptance criteria and a proposed payment/inspection milestone schedule. Ben — please flag any billing ops implications for the pilot credits.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Globex RFP: Implementation questionnaire and desired migration timeline

Marissa / team —

This is excellent, thank you all. The timeline looks achievable and the technical checklist covers our main concerns. A couple of follow-ups before we close this section:

1) Can you formalize the canary schedule into the CSV template you mentioned and include an example ramp (we want the exact timing and traffic percentages per day).
2) For the audit logs: can you confirm retention options (90 / 365 / custom) and whether logs can be mirrored to our SIEM in near real-time?
3) Please include the SOC 2 Type II report (or link) and the DPIA sample referenced — prod/legal will need this to move to redline.

If you can return the canary CSV + SOC 2 link by end of day tomorrow we’ll mark this section green and move to the commercial redlines.

Regards,
Henry Li
Director, Vendor Evaluation | Globex Financial
henry.li@globex.com
